cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet is still bringing the Lord GOD's message to Jerusalem. God has pictured her like a baby thrown out in an open field, whom He rescued and made His own, and then she turned to idols. Now He says everyone who speaks in proverbs will quote one about her: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

cards.question: The proverb says Jerusalem is just like her mother. What did her mother despise?

cards.text: And Jerusalem has sisters who despised their husbands and children too. The older one lives to her north, with her daughters.

cards.question: Who is Jerusalem's older sister, living to her north?
Jerusalem's younger sister, living to her south with her daughters, is ___.

cards.text: Samaria is the city where Ahab reigned over Israel (1 Kings 16:29). And Sodom is the city the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24).
Sodom. SODOM. Of every city in the Bible, friend, that is the LAST sister you want somebody comparing you to.

cards.question: Jerusalem walked in her sisters' ways and practiced their abominations. What does God say happened soon after?

answers.text: She became more depraved than they were
She turned and warned them to stop
She stayed just as bad as they were

cards.text: Then God says, 'As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD…' When He opens with THAT, friend, you lean in.

cards.question: True or false: God says Sodom and her daughters did worse than Jerusalem and her daughters.
God names Sodom's iniquity: she and her daughters were arrogant, overfed and complacent. What did they not do?

cards.text: Overfed and complacent. Friend, that's me after I taste-test a WHOLE tray, flat on my gold base like I'm never getting up again.
But this is no laughing matter. Sodom was haughty and committed abominations before God, so He removed them, as Jerusalem has seen.

cards.question: Now God turns to the older sister, Samaria. How do her sins compare to Jerusalem's?

answers.text: She did not commit half of them
She committed the very same ones

cards.question: Jerusalem multiplied her abominations so much that she made her sisters appear ___.

cards.text: That's like burning a batch so black that my LOPSIDED batch from last week suddenly looks like a prize winner. So does looking worse than everybody else get Jerusalem off the hook?

cards.question: True or false: Since her sisters appear more righteous, Jerusalem doesn't have to bear her disgrace.

cards.text: And then, friend, the message takes a turn I did NOT see coming. God says, 'But I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, as well as Samaria and her daughters.'

cards.question: True or false: God says He will restore Jerusalem along with Sodom and Samaria.
Jerusalem will be restored along with her sisters. What does God say she will bear when He does?

cards.text: Sodom and her daughters, and Samaria and her daughters, will return to their former state. And Jerusalem and her daughters will too.

cards.question: Then God asks a hard question. In the day of her pride, before her wickedness was uncovered, how did Jerusalem treat her sister Sodom?

cards.text: Now Jerusalem is the one being scorned, by the daughters of Edom, Esau's nation (Genesis 36:1), and by the daughters of the Philistines, who fought Israel in Goliath's day (1 Samuel 17:1).
It's like laughing at the guy whose phone goes off in a meeting, and then YOURS rings, LOUD. God says she will bear the consequences of her lewdness and her abominations.

cards.question: God says He will deal with Jerusalem according to her deeds. What did she despise?

answers.text: The oath by breaking the covenant
The law by ignoring the priests

cards.text: After all of that, you'd think the message ends right there. Then God says one little word: 'But.'

cards.question: Jerusalem broke the covenant. What does God say He will do with the covenant He made with her in the days of her youth?
God says the covenant He will establish with Jerusalem is ___.

cards.text: She broke the covenant, and He remembers it. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, let me tell you, being remembered is NO small thing.

cards.question: When Jerusalem receives her older and younger sisters, she will remember her ways and be ashamed. What will God give the sisters to her as?
True or false: God says He gives Jerusalem her sisters because of His covenant with her.
God says He will establish His covenant with Jerusalem. What will she know then?

cards.text: And then the very last promise in the message. God says He will make atonement for all she has done.

cards.question: When God makes atonement for all Jerusalem has done, she will remember and be ashamed. What will she never again do because of her disgrace?

cards.text: Jerusalem doesn't make the atonement, God does. And the city that once scorned her sister ends up with nothing left to say.

findings.problem: Card 3 cites Ezekiel 16:45-46, but the walkthrough never tells the end of 16:45: 'Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.' This is the line that explains the 'Like mother, like daughter' proverb, so the baker misses an important detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about Sodom. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. Card 6 already cites the same verse. Fold the joke into a card that tells part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about 'overfed and complacent' from 16:49, which card 11 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage. Card 13 then has to open with 'But this is no laughing matter' to undo it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card says the Philistines 'fought Israel in Goliath's day' and cites only 1 Samuel 17:1. That verse doesn't mention Goliath. He is introduced in 1 Samuel 17:4, so the reference doesn't support the fact.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This card recaps 16:59-60, which cards 8, 10 and 11 already covered, and adds a joke. It moves nothing forward. It also changes the tense: it says 'He remembers it', but the text says 'I will remember'.

Nothing sets up 'but not because of My covenant with you' (16:61). Cards 9 to 13 have just stressed God remembering and establishing the covenant, so a thoughtful baker would reason their way to 'True'. The right answer can only be reached by luck. Either give the story context first or ask a different question.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The last card cites 16:56-63 and only recaps what came before: who makes the atonement, and having nothing left to say. It tells nothing new.

The card ties Jerusalem's silence in 16:63 to her scorning of Sodom in 16:56 ('the city that once scorned her sister ends up with nothing left to say'). The text says she won't open her mouth 'because of your disgrace'. It never connects this to the scorn.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2: 7 of its 10 choice cards (3, 5, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17). There are only 2 true or false cards and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
